The gameplay loop

Turn a maze into a defense.

01

Place walls and towers

Shape an enemy route through your defenses.

02

Send the next wave

Release the authored enemy roster when you’re ready.

03

Fight with the drone

Fly and fire while towers use physics to knock enemies down or off course.

04

Repair, upgrade or sell

Reinvest between attacks and revise the layout.

Completely blocked enemies can attack walls or towers. Route design and combat effectiveness have to work together.

Why the mechanics matter

Physics turns a hit into
a control problem.

Knockback and recovery

Interrupt an enemy, displace it and account for its return to the fight.

Vehicles with physical bodies

Contacts, chassis geometry and walls influence movement and congestion.

A player-controlled drone

Fly, collide and switch among Pulse, Rockets, Railgun and Arc roles.

Direct-fire towers, rockets and Slapper knockback combine with mission-based drone weapon unlocks.

Challenge and replay

Each battlefield changes
the planning problem.

20 hours of gameplay, including campaign, challenges and all endless levels.

    SPEAKER NOTES

    Project details

    Game and project details

    The game and its editions

    20 hours of gameplay, including all endless levels. The full build includes 22 gameplay maps and a main menu, with campaign, challenges, maze construction, physics-based combat and a player-controlled drone.

    UE4.26.2: original human-written gameplay Blueprints and minimal C++ boilerplate.

    UE5.8.3: AI-assisted modernization combining native C++ gameplay, UI, tooling and tests with retained Blueprints.

    One original developer. The game source has never been public.

    Code and editable Blueprints

    28,296 C++ code lines across 181 files. Runtime systems: 17,999 lines; editor tooling: 3,092; tests: 7,205.

    UE4 contains 296 Blueprint-family packages; UE5 contains 274. Each edition has 134 Blueprint-family packages under Content/TowerD.

    Native systems cover targeting, movement, drone weapons, construction, collision, UI and upgrade logic. Project code totals exclude engine, plugin and generated intermediate code.

    Development history and training context

    Original development history begins February 16, 2019. Preserved UE4 history includes 43 unique commits, with 41 in the original branch. The UE5 branch contains 21 commits, with 28 across branches, remotes and tags.

    Git repositories, project backups from 2019, engineering documents, player feedback, reviews, development logs, surveys and Trello planning records accompany the game.

    UE5 AI development chats are available on request.

    AI testing and project content

    A purpose-built AI gameplay tester verifies levels through defense planning, tower purchases, upgrades, drone control and wave execution.

    The full tower-defense and UE5 unit/regression test suite includes 117 passing native tests and 7,205 lines across 39 test files. Automated runs record game state, outcomes and screenshots.

    Full Content libraries: 27.474 GB UE4 and 27.257 GB UE5. Windows distributions: 3.097 GB UE4 and 3.995 GB UE5. Bundled Content references: 2.802 GB and 3.759 GB.

    The source libraries include unused asset-pack content and Marketplace assets used in the game.
